transcript.text: induction hob keeps turnin off after 5-10 mins on high, have to keep restartin it. drives me nuts. any1 know y?

This is probably the hob's safety system kicking in. Induction hobs generate significant heat and have internal fans; if they can't cool themselves, or if the pan isn't transferring heat efficiently, they shut down to prevent damage. The most common causes are:
1. Blocked ventilation: Ensure nothing is covering the air vents (often at the front edge).
2. Pan issues: The pan must be flat-bottomed and large enough for the zone. If it's too small or magnetic material isn't sufficient, the hob detects this and cuts out. Please check these first. Also, does an error code (like 'E' followed by a number) appear on the display when it switches off?
pans r fine, proper induction ones. sometimes a small code flashes but i never catch what it says

Since the pans are fine, that flashing code is likely an error related to overheating protection (which kicks in if vents are blocked or the internal fan fails) or a sensor issue. To identify the exact meaning of that code and guide you safely, I need the brand and model number of your hob. It’s usually on a label on the underside of the unit or on the guarantee card.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
its a Samsung, dont know the model and not going to go looking under it. started after a new drawer unit was fitted under it last month tho

The timing with the new drawer unit is a strong clue. Induction hobs generate significant heat internally and rely on airflow to cool themselves. If the new cabinet is too high or blocks the ventilation slots (often at the front edge), the hob will overheat and shut down as a safety measure after 5–10 minutes. Please check if there is at least a 5cm gap between the top of that drawer unit and the bottom of your hob. If it’s tight, try lifting the hob slightly (if possible) or removing the cabinet door to see if airflow improves. If you hear a fan running inside when you turn it on but it still cuts out, the internal cooling fan may have failed, which would require an engineer.
not lifting the hob or taking the drawer off, not doing that. fan does roar before it cuts out tho. so is it an engineer job?

Yes, this sounds like an engineer job. The fact that you hear the fan roaring before it cuts out suggests the system is trying to cool itself but failing—likely because the internal heat sink is blocked with dust or the fan isn't moving enough air despite running. Since opening the hob involves mains wiring and accessing live components, I can't advise you to dismantle it yourself. Please call a qualified appliance engineer to inspect the internal cooling system and clean or replace the faulty part.

candidates: Overheating protection triggered by blocked ventilation or a failing cooling fan (high)
Pan compatibility issue (pan too small, wrong material, or not sitting flat) (medium)
Faulty temperature sensor or main PCB overheating (low)
